//: Named `nav` to match its Module Federation name and directory; it was `search`, a leftover from the single-spa starter this package was copied from.
name: nav
//deps: No framework runtime, and no `single-spa` either. The chrome is mounted on every route, so anything it depends on is paid for on first paint by every visitor — see README.md. The single-spa adapter is `src/lifecycles.ts`, and it is short because a custom element's connect/disconnect already IS the lifecycle contract.
//design-system: A real dependency: the bar renders `<mm-button>`, so the components must be registered at runtime, not just their CSS tokens present. Lit rides along transitively and is a federation singleton (see webpack.config.js) — the shell already has it on the page for `calendar` and `auth`, so the marginal cost to first paint is nil, and a chrome that hand-rolled its own button would be the most visible thing in the app to drift from the theme.
